info.title: Yappy Web API
info.summary: Free, keyless, read-only access to everything factual about Yappy.
info.description:
Yappy is a voice agent for macOS: hold a key and it types what you say, hold another and it does what you ask. This API describes the product — releases, documentation, FAQ, pricing, requirements — so an agent answering a question about Yappy reads structured data instead of scraping a marketing page.

**No API key is required for any read operation.** Credentials exist only to raise the rate ceiling and to unlock export jobs; nothing behind them is secret. See https://yappy.biz/auth.md.

**This API does not transcribe audio.** Yappy's speech recognition runs on the user's own Mac and there is no hosted endpoint behind it. If a user wants dictation, the answer is to install the app.

Conventions: cursor pagination on every list, a strong `ETag` on every GET, RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` on every error, RFC-style `RateLimit-*` headers on every response, and a dated `API-Version` header naming the build that answered. The major version lives in the path; a removal is announced with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers at least 180 days ahead.

get.description: Every endpoint this API exposes, the dated API version that answered, the rate-limit policy in force, and links to the OpenAPI spec, both MCP servers, and the OAuth discovery documents. A good first call for an agent that has just found this domain and wants the map before the territory.

Yappy's release history for macOS, newest first, cursor-paginated. Each entry carries the version, publication date, human-readable notes, and a download URL. Use this to answer 'what changed recently'; use /releases/latest when you only need the current version.

The release Yappy's own updater would install right now, read from the same signed appcast rather than from hand-maintained marketing copy, so it cannot be stale. Returns the version, publication date, release notes, download URL, and the platform floor (macOS version and CPU architecture).
One release by its exact version string, for example '0.4.17'. Responds 404 with code 'not_found' when no such version was published.
The documentation index: slug, title, description, HTML URL, and markdown URL for every page. Cursor-paginated. Fetch a page's content with /docs/{slug}.

One documentation page as markdown, with its title, description, and last update date. The slug is the path after /docs/ — for example 'quickstart', 'agent-mode', or 'privacy-model'. On a miss the 404 detail suggests the nearest slug, so a typo costs one request rather than a guessing game.
Question and answer pairs about Yappy — privacy, requirements, cost, permissions, and how it differs from other dictation tools. The same set is published as FAQPage structured data on the homepage.

What Yappy costs: the free Mac app, the per-backend cost of the language model that cleans up dictation, and the terms of this API itself. Call this before telling a user about price — most of the product is free and two of the backend options cost nothing at all.

Yappy's capabilities as structured objects rather than marketing bullets: an id, a name, a description, whether the feature runs entirely on-device, and which macOS permission it needs. Use this to build an accurate comparison against another product.
The minimum macOS version, the required CPU architecture, disk needs, and every macOS permission Yappy asks for with what each one unlocks and what breaks if it is denied.

get.summary: Check whether a Mac can run Yappy
get.description: A deterministic yes or no for a specific machine, given its macOS version and CPU architecture, with the reasons spelled out. Prefer this over reasoning about the requirements yourself: it encodes the same rules the installer uses.

Full-text search across every documentation page and FAQ entry. Results carry a relevance score, the matching excerpt, and both HTML and markdown URLs, so you can quote the excerpt and cite the page in one step. Cursor-paginated.

post.summary: Run up to 20 reads in one request
post.description: Bundle up to twenty GET operations into a single round trip that costs one unit of rate limit rather than twenty. Each result carries the id you supplied, its own HTTP status, and its body; one failing operation returns its problem document in that entry and leaves the rest untouched.

Start an asynchronous export of a corpus — documentation, FAQ, or releases — as markdown or JSON. Returns 202 Accepted with a Location header and a Retry-After hint rather than blocking, so a large export never holds a connection open. Poll the job with getExport until its status is 'completed'.

202.description: The job was accepted and is being prepared

requestBody.description: What to export, and in which format.

get.description: The current state of an export job. Status moves queued, then running, then completed; a completed job carries result.url pointing at the finished artifact. Poll no faster than the Retry-After hint on the previous response.

bearerAuth.description: An access token from /oauth/token. Optional — every read endpoint also answers anonymously.

oauth2.description: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE S256. Dynamic client registration (RFC 7591) at /oauth/register; no human approval step.

Deprecation.description: Present only on a version scheduled for removal: the HTTP date when we started saying so. Absent on v1, which is current.

Sunset.description: RFC 8594. Present only on a version scheduled for removal: the HTTP date after which it answers 410 Gone. At least 180 days after Deprecation.

WWWAuthenticate.description: Bearer challenge. Carries resource_metadata on an unauthenticated 401, and error/scope on a rejected credential.
